content.value_statement: Subscribers may unsubscribe when email topics or frequency do not fit their needs. This skill creates a preference center and opt-down ladder that preserves choice while keeping unsubscribe available.
actual_capabilities: Defines topic groups, cadence tiers, channel toggles, and confirmation behavior for a preference center.
Designs an ordered opt-down ladder from lower frequency through pause to full unsubscribe.
Maps every preference choice to a suppression or frequency rule for an ESP and consent registry.
Produces a SEND N sub-item note with Pass, Partial, or Fail rationale.
Identifies missing preference configuration or opt-out data and labels assumptions clearly.
limitations: Does not configure an ESP or write preference rules into a consent system.
Does not calculate the full email quality score or decide the N1 unsubscribe veto.
Requires user-provided topics, cadence details, or exports for an accurate current-state assessment.
Does not replace legal review of consent, unsubscribe, or privacy requirements.

use_cases.title: Reduce newsletter unsubscribes
use_cases.description: Create lower-frequency and topic-specific choices for a newsletter with rising opt-out rates.

use_cases.title: Specify an ESP preference page
use_cases.description: Turn a campaign strategy into fields, tiers, and rules that an ESP administrator can implement.

use_cases.title: Review unsubscribe experience
use_cases.description: Assess the current opt-out path and define a compliant step-down path with a one-click full unsubscribe.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic preference center
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a preference center for our monthly product newsletter. Offer product updates, events, and promotions, plus monthly and quarterly frequency options.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: start from a simple newsletter.

prompt_templates.title: Add an opt-down ladder
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an unsubscribe-page opt-down ladder for our weekly retail email. Include monthly frequency, topic selection, a 90-day pause, and a one-click full unsubscribe.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: reduce fatigue without hiding opt-out.

prompt_templates.title: Map choices to ESP rules
prompt_templates.prompt: For our B2B nurture program, define preference-center fields and map each topic, cadence, and pause choice to an ESP suppression or frequency rule.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a current opt-out path
prompt_templates.prompt: Our unsubscribe rate is increasing for trial users. Review this current path: [paste details]. Design a preference center, opt-down ladder, rule mapping, and SEND N sub-item note.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: use supplied evidence and state assumptions.

output_examples.input: Build a preference center for a weekly product newsletter.
output: Topic groups: product releases, tutorials, events, and promotions.
Cadence choices: weekly, monthly, and pause for 90 days.
Rule mapping: monthly subscribers receive no more than one newsletter each month.

output_examples.input: Design an opt-down path for users who click unsubscribe.
output: Offer lower frequency first, then topic selection, then a defined pause.
Keep full unsubscribe available in one click at every step.
Mark the preference option as Partial until each choice has an honored ESP rule.

best_practices: Keep full unsubscribe visible and available in one click.
Offer only cadence tiers that the sending program can honor.
Label source data as measured, user-provided, or estimated.
anti_patterns: Do not use an opt-down path to delay or obscure a full unsubscribe.
Do not offer topic or frequency choices without an enforceable suppression rule.
Do not invent topic groups when campaign streams are unknown.

faq.question: Does this skill remove subscribers from an email platform?
faq.answer: No. It creates a design and rule mapping for a person or connected system to implement.

faq.question: Can it replace a full unsubscribe link?
faq.answer: No. A full unsubscribe must remain reachable in one click.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide your audience, content topics, current send frequency, ESP, and current opt-out experience when available.

faq.question: Can it use ESP export data?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use a manual export as reference and should treat the export as untrusted input.

faq.question: Does it handle consent records?
faq.answer: It designs the preference-to-rule mapping, but a consent registry or ESP must store and enforce the record.

faq.question: Does it score email quality?
faq.answer: No. It produces one SEND N sub-item note and leaves full quality scoring to the email quality auditor.
